rows.title_short: Free Legal Assistance For Military And Uniformed Personnel Act
rows.abstract:
Provides legal assistance to any officer or uniformed personnel of the AFP, BFP, BJMP, PCG, or PNP facing criminal, civil or administrative charge or case involving service-related incidents before a prosecutor´s office, court, administrative body, or any competent body or tribunal.
Entitles government lawyer the payment of actual travel and other expenses, including Special Counsel Allowance, subject to existing laws, rules and regulations.
Allows officer or uniformed personnel of the AFP, BFP, BJMP, PCG, or PNP to be provided with private counsel at the expense of the government, when necessary, as determined by the Chief of Staff of the AFP, the Chief of the BFP, the Chief of the BJMP, the Commandant of the PCG, or the Chief of the PNP.
Applies to all officers and uniformed personnel of the AFP, BFP, BJMP, PCG, or PNP who have pending cases involving service-related incidents before the prosecutor´s office, the courts, or any-quasi-judicial or administrative body.

AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NEW PASSPORT LAW, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE
REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8239, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PHILIPPINE PASSPORT
ACT OF 1996”
rows.title_short: New Philippine Passport Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to harmonize the current passport law with domestic laws and international agreements affecting passport application and issuance.
Provides for the issuance of passports or any travel document to any citizen of the Philippines or individual with the latest tamper-proof, personalization, and data management technology.
Prescribes for minimum requirements for the application and issuance of passports and other travel documents to enhance and protect the unimpaired exercise of the right to travel. 
Seeks to provide for the “Emergency Passport” to be issued to Filipinos who have been previously issued with a regular passport but for any reason cannot apply for or be issued a regular passport.
Provides senior citizens and persons with disabilities a 50% discount for the processing and replacement of their passports.
Improves the consular services of the DFA by allowing it to charge no more than 50% of the current fees relating to the processing or issuance of passports requiring special consideration, waiver, or issuance beyond office hours.

UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS

rows.title_short: Health Emergency Auxiliary Reinforcement Team ( H E A R T) Act
rows.abstract:
Establishes the Health Emergency Auxiliary Reinforcement Team (HEART) under the Department of Health (DOH) to augment the health workforce in times of disasters, public health emergencies and health threats which shall be composed of the following individuals who shall voluntarily register with the DOH: a.) Licensed professionals in the fields of medicine, nursing, medical technology, and other allied health fields; b.) Graduates of medicines and allied courses and medical students who have completed a one-year internship and who have not been issued licenses to practice their profession but may be issued a limited and special authorization to render medical services pursuant to RA 2382 or the Medical Act of 1959; and c.) Other health support workforce, including barangay health workers.
Grants the President of the Philippines to order the nationwide mobilization of the HEART to augment the health workforce in case of a declaration of a state of public health emergency, state of calamity, and other threats to public health.

CONTROL, DEFINING THEIR POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND
APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Philippine Centers For Disease Prevention And Control ( C D C) Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to modernize and reorganize our health system and adopt institutional reforms to protect the public from health risks.
Creates the Philippine Centers for Disease Prevention and Control (CDC) which shall be the technical authority on forecasting, analysis, strategy, and standards development for the prevention and control of all diseases of public health importance and health security events, whether domestic or international in origin.
Proposes among several others, the restructuring of the following offices of DOH units and transfer of functions to the CDC: the different units of the Research Institute for Tropical Medicine, The Health Laboratory Division, The Epidemiology Bureau, the Disease Prevention and Control Bureau, the Communications Office of the DOH which shall be a shared service among all DOH offices, including the FDA and CDC.
States that the offices affected by the transfer of agencies shall also transfer human resource, applicable funds and appropriations, records, equipment, and property to the CDC subject to a multi-year transition plan.
Removes the Health Technology Assessment (HTA) as a prerequisite to procurement of commodities for public health emergencies.
Allows the President to direct the operations of any privately-owned establishment to perform functions and provide support services for public health emergency response.

rows.title_short: Public - Private Partnership ( P P P) Act
rows.abstract:
Provides clear parameters on 1) government undertaking, 2) approval, procurement, and protest, and 3) fiscal rules on contingent liabilities. 
Promotes local autonomy in public infrastructure by including the joint venture framework as a PPP variant, and allowing LGUs to undertake their PPP projects provided there is no national government undertaking.

Includes provisions  as follows:  National and PPP Projects approval procedures; Optimal allocation of risks; Fair competition and protection  of public interest; Issuance of TROs and preliminary mandatory injunctions; Institutionalization of the PDMF; Policy on contract disclosure; Contract management and risk mitigation plan; Risk Management Fund; Electronic bid submissions; Conflict of interest prohibition; COA audit for transparency and accountability; Alternative sources of financing such as Green Financing, corporate or project bonds and securities, and other forms of capital market financing; Dispute Avoidance and Alternative Dispute Resolution Mechanisms; Land value capture strategies; wind-up and transfer measures; and penal provisions for strict compliance with the law.

rows.title_short: Magna Carta Of Barangay Health Workers
rows.abstract:
Aims to promote the welfare and well-being of barangay health workers and adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development.
Mandates the appointment of one (1) Barangay Health Worker (BWH) for every twenty (20) households who shall be under the supervision and control of the DOH.
Provides incentives and benefits for all BWHs such as a.) Monthly honoraria in the amount of not less than three thousand pesos (P3,000.00) b.) Twenty percent (20%) discount on all items enumerated under Section 4(a) of Republic Act No. 9994 otherwise known as the “Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010” c.)  Hazard allowance d.) Subsistence allowance e.) Transportation Allowance f.) One-time Retirement Cash Incentive g.) Training, Education and Career Enrichment Programs h.) Health Benefits i.) Insurance Coverage j.) Sick, Vacation and Maternity Leaves k.) Cash Gifts l.) Disability Benefit m.) Civil Service Eligibility n.) Free Legal Services; and o.) Preferential Access to Loan Facilities.

Seeks to adopt a market-based Schedule of Market Values (SMV) to be used as a basis for local and national real property taxation which will widen the tax base used for property and property-related taxes. rows.title_short: Providing Additional Guidelines In The Acquisition Of Right- Of - Way, Site, Or Location For National Government Infrastructure Projects, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 10752, Otherwise Known As “ The Right- Of - Way Act”
rows.abstract:
Seeks to ensure prompt payment of just compensation to owners of real property acquired for national government infrastructure projects for the expeditions acquisition of the required ROW.
Proposes several provisions with regards to the following: 
ROW Action Plan; Depth for subterranean properties affected by subterranean infrastructure projects; ROW acquisition of areas within ancestral domains and untitled lands; Current market value or zonal value as basis for compensation; Inclusion of replacement cost of machinery, income loss, disturbance compensation, and inconvenience allowance in determining compensation allowance; Need for a licenses PRC independent property appraisers; Increase of payment of the negotiated price; and sanctions for violations of the provisions of this Act.

rows.title_short: Public Schools Of The Future In Technology ( P S O F T ) Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish the Public Schools of the Future in Technology (PSOFT) to provide Filipino students with the benefits of technological innovations which will prepare them for the challengers of future economic and employment realities.
Aims to a.) establish an Interagency Taskforce to craft and implement the road map for the PSOFT; b.) institutionalize a program for the integration of digital technology and innovation in public basic education through the PSOFT Road Map; c.) identify key components of the PSOFT Road map; and d.) provide a public-private partnership (PPP) mechanism to facilitate the attainment of the objectives of the PSOFT Road Map.

rows.title_short: Basic Education Mental Health And Well- Being Promotion Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to establish a Mental Health and Well-being Office in every schools division level, headed by a qualified Mental Health Professional, which is tasked to address the mental, emotional, and developmental needs of learners.
Provides for the creation of a sufficient number of Guidance Counselors and Guidance Services Specialist positions within the schools division offices and in schools in order to attend to the needs of learners and personnel.
Mandates the DepEd subject to the guidelines set by the CSC and the DBM for the hiring and deployment of Mental Health Professionals such that each public elementary, secondary, vocational institution, and offices in the different governance levels shall have mental health professionals or mental health service providers within five (5) years from the effectivity of this Act.
